intro: Mississippi runs its elections county by county, through the circuit clerk and a county election commission, with municipal clerks for city elections.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID to vote at the polls or in person at the circuit clerk's office. Accepted IDs include a Mississippi driver's license, a U.S. passport, a military photo ID, a tribal photo ID, and a current student photo ID from a Mississippi college. If you forget your ID, you can vote by affidavit ballot and show an ID at the circuit clerk's office within five business days. Free voter ID cards are available at any circuit clerk's office.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: In-person absentee voting
dates.detail: You can vote absentee in person at your circuit clerk's office on weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm. Offices are also open 8 am to noon on Saturday, Oct. 24 and Saturday, Oct. 31. You must meet one of the reasons in Mississippi law, such as being 65 or older, having a disability, or being away from home on Election Day. The last day is Oct. 31.

dates.detail: The circuit clerk must receive a mailed absentee ballot by 5 pm on this date, within five business days of the election. The ballot must also have been postmarked by Election Day.
